title: Bunch of AI tools for Investing
author: AcanthocephalaNo6605
selftext:
I recently asked a question that how everyone is utilizing AI in trading although its not deterministic. I got the same answer from everyone that they dont utilize it for trading but for research and come up with thesis easily.

I guess investing is better positioned to use the AI, but when I am searching for all the available tools..... there are a lot and I am not exaggerating but there are a lot but non of them has made a mark on larger user-base.

What are some of the tools you guys are using. Are you using anything specific or claude/gemini/gpt are no brainer.

Even if you are using some tools or generic LLM where is the pain point that you as a investor or stock researcher feel needs to be solved.

I am figuring our role of AI in financial markets which are highly deterministic and regulated.

comments.author: SeanStock
comments.body:
I let it trade for me. I created a series of research skills and an allocator, and have been letting it do it's thing for a few weeks. Mostly for fun, but I wanted a portfolio built to capture long-tail supply chain stocks in the AI space, and given the research space is narrow I don't think I am going to do a better job than Opus. I don't want to learn about every data center water circulation system manufacturer. Just own a piece of them. 

[aishovels.fyi](http://aishovels.fyi)

Sorry, the sites slow, it's a personal project and the box has a lot on it.

comments.author: The_AI_Trader
comments.body:
You should look into AI Trading Agents.   
  
Putting ourselves in control of agents, instead of staring at charts all day, allows us to manage risk and become the fund managers. Let the AI do the thinking. We then move to managing the risk side of things, and which AI traders to perform. Look into SkyAnalyst AI.   


AS far as overall platforms, Claude tends to have the upper hand for more overview of markets. Unless you build a platform that can give all the realtime data the LLM needs in order to properly give trading advice. It's limited by the data it crawls through the web. It's not like it can't do the trade, it's the data limitation. Hence why platforms like the one I mentioned, based on Claude , can do what they do.   


Best of luck! AI trading forever lol!
